candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record emphasizes progressive 2-year course, spindle cells with storiform arrangement in deep dermis, and lesion sizes up to 4 cm with mucosal involvement — hallmarks of PNHC rather than JXG. While both are non-Langerhans cell histiocytoses with overlapping immunoprofile, PNHC is a recognized distinct entity. JXG typically regresses spontaneously and lacks the prominent spindle cell/storiform deep dermal component described here. The candidate asserts a related but incompatible subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Juvenile xanthogranuloma (JXG) shares histological features (Touton cells, foamy histiocytes, CD68+/CD163+/S100-/CD1a-) but is a distinct non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis entity; progressive nodular histiocytosis (PNHC) is characterized by progressive lifelong accumulation of nodules, spindle cell component with storiform collagen arrangement in deep dermis, and lack of spontaneous regression — features that distinguish it from JXG

case_quality_flags: PNHC and disseminated JXG share significant histological overlap; distinction rests on clinical course (progressive vs. self-resolving) and deep dermal spindle cell storiform pattern favoring PNHC
